attempts.cause: T005_STOCK_UTIL.available function does not account for products that have never been reserved, leading to an incorrect return of 0 instead of the on_hand quantity.
attempts.candidate:
create or replace package body t005_stock_util as
  -- Units of a product that can still be reserved (on hand minus reserved).
  function available(p_product_id in number) return number is
    l_available number;
  begin
    select on_hand - NVL(reserved, 0)
      into l_available
      from t005_stock
     where product_id = p_product_id;
    return l_available;
  exception
    when no_data_found then
      -- If product does not exist in t005_stock, it has 0 on_hand and 0 reserved, so available is 0.
      -- However, based on the failing test, if it has never been reserved, it implies it exists but reserved is null/not set.
      -- If it truly doesn't exist, 0 is correct. If it exists but has no reservation record, the select above should handle it if reserved is nullable.
      -- The original code returned 0 on no_data_found. If the product exists but has no reservation, the select should succeed if reserved is nullable.
      -- The fix is to use NVL in the select statement to handle the case where reserved is NULL, which is what the test implies is failing for new products.
      return 0;
  end available;
end t005_stock_util;
/
